items: Uttarakhand was formed on 9 November 2000 as the 27th state of India.
Formerly known as Uttaranchal; renamed Uttarakhand on 1 January 2007.
Capital: Dehradun (temporary); Summer capital: Gairsain (Bhararisain), declared 2020.
Area: 53,483 sq km | Population (2011): ~1.01 crore | Density: 189/sq km.
Borders: China (N), Nepal (E), Himachal Pradesh (W), Uttar Pradesh (S).
2 Divisions: Garhwal (HQ Pauri) and Kumaon (HQ Nainital).
13 Districts: 7 in Garhwal, 6 in Kumaon.
Largest district by area: Chamoli (8030 sq km).
Smallest district by area: Champawat (1766 sq km).
Most populous district: Haridwar; least populous: Rudraprayag.
Vidhan Sabha: 70 seats (unicameral); Lok Sabha: 5 seats; Rajya Sabha: 3 seats.
First CM: Nityanand Swami (BJP); Current CM: Pushkar Singh Dhami (BJP).
Governors of UK: Started with Surjit Singh Barnala; current: Lt Gen Gurmit Singh.
High Court of Uttarakhand is at Nainital (est. Nov 9, 2000).
UKPSC and UKSSSC both headquartered in Haridwar.
Nanda Devi (7816 m) — highest peak entirely within India; in Chamoli.
Kamet (7756 m) — 2nd highest peak in Uttarakhand.
Char Dham: Yamunotri → Gangotri → Kedarnath → Badrinath.
Ganga forms at Devprayag (Bhagirathi + Alaknanda).
Bhagirathi originates from Gaumukh, Gangotri Glacier (Uttarkashi).
Yamuna originates from Yamunotri Glacier, Uttarkashi.
Panch Prayag (upstream to downstream): Vishnuprayag, Nandaprayag, Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag, Devprayag.
Panch Kedar: Kedarnath, Tungnath, Rudranath, Madhyamaheshwar, Kalpeshwar.
Tungnath (3680 m) — highest Shiva temple in the world; in Rudraprayag.
Panch Badri: Badrinath (main), Yogadhyan Badri, Bridha Badri, Bhavisya Badri, Adi Badri.
Jim Corbett NP (1936) — First national park of India; originally Hailey NP.
Gangotri NP — Largest NP in UK (2390 sq km); Uttarkashi district.
Nanda Devi NP + Valley of Flowers NP — UNESCO Natural World Heritage Sites.
Hemkund Sahib — Sikh pilgrimage at 4329 m; Chamoli; surrounded by 7 peaks.
State Animal: Alpine Musk Deer | State Bird: Himalayan Monal.
State Tree: Buransh/Rhododendron | State Flower: Brahma Kamal.
State Fish: Golden Mahseer.
Chipko Movement (1973) — started at Reni village, Chamoli; Gaura Devi led.
Sundarlal Bahuguna — Padma Vibhushan; Chipko movement leader.
Chandi Prasad Bhatt — Ramon Magsaysay Award 1982; Chipko Movement.
Over 12,000 Van Panchayats in UK manage ~5 lakh hectares of community forests.
IIT Roorkee (est. 1847) — oldest technical institution in Asia.
G.B. Pant University, Pantnagar (1960) — First agricultural university in India.
LBSNAA, Mussoorie — IAS training academy.
FRI, Dehradun — Forest Research Institute; deemed university; colonial campus.
NIM, Uttarkashi (1965) — Nehru Mountaineering Institute.
WII, Dehradun — Wildlife Institute of India; premier wildlife research body.
ONGC exploration HQ is in Dehradun.
SIDCUL industrial corridors: Haridwar (BHEL, Patanjali, Hero, Tata) and Pantnagar (Bajaj, Britannia).
Tehri Dam — on Bhagirathi; 1000 MW Stage I; Tehri Garhwal.
Rishikesh-Karnprayag Railway (under construction) — 125 km; 17 tunnels.
Char Dham All-Weather Road Project — major national highway expansion.
Aipan — Traditional Kumaoni rice-paste folk art; GI tagged.
Chholiya — Kumaoni sword and shield dance at weddings.
Harela — Kumaon harvest/sowing festival in Shravan (July).
Phool Dei — Kumaon spring festival in Chaitra (March); girls scatter flowers.
Uttarayani Mela, Bageshwar — Begar abolition 1921; Badridutt Pandey.
Devidhura Mela, Champawat — Bagwal (stone pelting) festival; Shravan Purnima.
Jauljibi Mela, Pithoragarh — India-Nepal border trade fair; November.
Nanda Devi Raj Jat Yatra — held every 12 years; 280 km procession.
Kumbh Mela — Haridwar; every 12 years (Purna Kumbh); Ganga bank.
Sumitranandan Pant — born Kausani, Almora; Hindi poet; Jnanpith awardee.
Govind Ballabh Pant — born Almora; India's Home Minister; Bharat Ratna.
Vir Chandra Singh Garhwali — refused to fire on Pathans, Peshawar 1930.
Tilari Massacre (May 30, 1930) — Tehri Garhwal; compared to Jallianwala Bagh.
Rampur Tiraha firing (Oct 2, 1994) — Muzaffarnagar; Krantiveer Shaurya Diwas.
Gairsain (Bhararisain) declared summer capital in March 2020.
Uttarakhand passed the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in February 2024 — first state in India.
Roopkund Lake (Chamoli, 4800 m) — Mystery Lake with skeletal remains.
Gangotri Glacier (30+ km) — largest glacier in Uttarakhand; source of Bhagirathi.
Nainital — most famous tourist lake; 2084 m altitude; Naini Devi temple.
Kainchi Dham, Bhowali — Neem Karoli Baba ashram; visited by Steve Jobs.
Jageshwar, Almora — 124 stone temples; Nagara style; 7th–14th century.
Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana — free health coverage up to Rs 5 lakh per family.
Mukhyamantri Vatsalya Yojana — Rs 3000/month to COVID-orphaned children till age 21.
Parvatmala Scheme — ropeway development at pilgrimage & hill sites.
Kumaon Kesari — title of Badridutt Pandey; anti-Begar movement leader.
Sex ratio in UK: 963 per 1000 males (above national average of 940).
Literacy rate: 78.82% | Male: 87.40% | Female: 70.01%.
Lipulekh Pass — India-Nepal-China trijunction; Kailash-Mansarovar route; Pithoragarh.
Mana village (Chamoli) — last Indian village before China border; near Badrinath.
Doodhatoli Hills — origin of Western Ramganga; Jim Corbett Park river.
Pindari Glacier — famous trekking glacier; source of Pindar river; Bageshwar.
Berinag tea (Champawat/Pithoragarh) — quality orthodox tea; GI indication pending.
Malta orange — Kumaon specialty citrus; Pithoragarh-Champawat.
Jhora/Jhori — circular group folk dance of Kumaon; harvest season.
Langvir Nritya — acrobatic Garhwali dance on poles.
Hudka — traditional drum of Kumaon folk music.
Dhol-Damau — ceremonial drum pair; Shilpkar (artisan) community tradition.
G.B. Pant National Himalayan Environment Institute — located at Kosi-Katarmal, Almora.
Uttarakhand has the highest proportion of forest cover (~71%) among larger Indian states.
Jolly Grant Airport (Dehradun) — main commercial airport; named after civil aviation pioneer.
Objective questions in competitive exams frequently test direct facts found in one-liner revision sets.
Pay special attention to precise names, dates, and technical keywords during rapid revision.

items: Quick revision one-liners synthesize key topics into high-yield statements for rapid review.
Regular review of concise factual points aids immediate retention and quick recall in objective exams.
Mastering core terminology and definitions serves as a strong foundation for competitive exam preparation.
